content:
Insurers keep pointing AI at underwriting. Trust gets won or lost in claims.

Claims typically eat 60 to 70% of P/C premiums, according to the U.S. Treasury. That's where the money goes, where regulators look, and where customers find out whether the policy they paid for actually means anything.

Yet claims still run on heroics. Good adjusters work around broken processes, and the outcome too often depends on who picks up the file.

AI should replace the heroics, not the adjusters. Vision models can assess catastrophe damage in minutes. Predictive models can flag bottlenecks days before they hit. Anomaly detection can catch fraud rings that look clean one claim at a time.

The goal isn't to become digital. It's to become reliable under stress.

Over the next decade, insurers will be judged less by how smartly they price risk and more by how consistently they honor it.

My latest for Carrier Management:
https://lnkd.in/eax6MAVv

#Insurance #InsurTech #AI #Claims #RiskManagement
comment: Automation only earns trust if claimants can challenge its decisions and reach a human when needed. Faster settlements mean little if errors become harder to contest.
